Evaluate an interpolant in a point

Source: R/interpolant.R
interpolant.Rd

An interpolant is a function returned by ipol() which has prespecified values in some points, and which fills in between with some reasonable values.

Arguments

x

The argument of the function. A function of more than one variable takes a vector. x can also be a matrix of column vectors.

threads

The number of threads to use for evaluation. All interpolants created by chebpol are parallelized. If given a matrix argument x, the vectors can be evaluated in parallel.

...

Other parameters. Currently used for simplex linear interpolants with the logical argument epol which makes the interpolant extrapolate to points outside the domain. The "stalker", "hstalker", "oldstalker", "multilinear" and "simplexlinear" interpolants have the argument blend, one of "linear", "cubic", "sigmoid", "parodic" and "square", which chooses the blending function described in vignette("stalker"). "stalker", "hstalker" and "simplexlinear" also take "mean". The default is "cubic" for "stalker" and "hstalker", and "linear" for the others.

Value

A numeric. If more than one point was evaluated, a vector.

Details

Interpolants have class chebpol_interpolant and the attributes method, the interpolation method, arity, the number of variables, and domain, a data frame with one row per variable and the columns name, lower and upper. The variables take their names from grid, dims, intervals or the row names of knots, and are named X1, X2, ... otherwise. Printing an interpolant shows these together with the defaults of its extra arguments, such as blend.

Examples

grid <- list(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 10), y = seq(0, 1, length.out = 10))
val <- runif(100)
dim(val) <- c(10, 10)
ip <- ipol(val, grid = grid, method = "fh")
ip
#> <chebpol_interpolant> fh, 2 variables
#> Domain: [0, 1] x [0, 1]
ip(c(0.3, 0.8))
#> [1] 0.6969905
ip(matrix(runif(12), 2), threads = 2)
#> [1] 0.2505217 1.2011162 1.2852535 0.6764973 1.0305336 1.3035894
